title: His is the kingdom, His is the praise.
subtitle: The last of the surahs that open with glorification

row.title: He wills, it happens
sub: and He is praised for it

then: Ibn Kathir notes this is the last of the surahs that begin with glorification. {idea}His is the dominion and to Him belongs the praise.{/idea} Whatever He wills happens without resistance, and whatever He does not will never happens.
now: The job offer fell through. The flight was cancelled. The test result came back fine. You call it luck, good or bad. {idea}Every one of those was decided by the King who is also praised for His decisions.{/idea}
old: Most of what happens to me is just chance.
new: Everything is in the hands of One who owns it all and deserves praise for it.
try: Next time something goes unexpectedly today, good or bad, say alhamdulillah before you react.

title: He created you, and you choose belief or denial.
subtitle: Same Creator, different answers, all seen
then: Allah says He created people, and among them are believers and disbelievers. Ibn Kathir says Allah sees who deserves guidance and who does not, and {idea}He is the Witness over every deed{/idea} and will repay it fully.
now: Two siblings, same house, same parents, same mosque. One prays, one has drifted. You might be either one, on different days. {idea}The verse does not end with the labels.{/idea} {reward}It ends with: He sees what you do.{/reward}
old: Whether I believe is just how I was raised.
new: The same Creator made us all, and He watches what each of us does with it.
try: Do one act today that you would be glad for Allah to see, without telling anyone.

title: He shaped you, and made your shape good.
subtitle: A body designed with care, a world made with purpose
then: Ibn Kathir says the heavens and earth were made {idea}with fairness and wisdom{/idea}, not for nothing. Allah shaped people in the best forms, as another verse says: He fashioned you and gave you proportion. And {idea}to Him is the return{/idea}.
now: You stand in front of the bathroom mirror counting flaws. You compare your face to filtered faces on your phone. {reward}Allah says He shaped you and made your shape good.{/reward} {idea}That body is a trust you carry back to Him.{/idea}
old: My body is something to fix and compare.
new: My form was made good by Allah, and I will return it to Him.
try: Next time you look in the mirror, name one thing about your body you are grateful for and say alhamdulillah.

title: He knows what you hide and what you show.
subtitle: Nothing in the chest is private from Him
then: After creation and the return, the passage ends on knowledge. Ibn Kathir says Allah informs of {idea}His knowledge of all that is in the heavens, the earth and the souls{/idea}. He knows what is concealed and what is revealed.
now: You smile at the colleague you resent. You donate and quietly hope someone notices. You scroll something at 2am that you would never admit to. {idea}None of it is hidden from Him.{/idea} {reward}And He still invites you back.{/reward}
old: My private thoughts are only mine.
new: Allah knows what is in my chest, so I want it to be worth seeing.
try: Notice one hidden motive behind something you do today, and quietly correct it for Allah.

title: Did the news of those before not reach you?
subtitle: History is a warning letter
then: The surah now turns to those who refused the message. Ibn Kathir says Allah reminds them of past nations who {trap}tasted the evil results of their denial and sins{/trap} in this world, with a painful punishment still to come after.
now: You read about someone who lost their family through a habit, or a company that fell through greed. You shake your head and scroll on. {idea}Those stories are letters addressed to you.{/idea} {reward}The ending can still be different for you.{/reward}
old: Stories of the past are interesting but not about me.
new: Every story of those before me is a warning I can still learn from.
try: Think of one person whose mistake you have seen up close. Write down the one lesson you want to keep.

title: Shall a mere human guide us?
subtitle: Rejecting the message because of the messenger
then: Ibn Kathir says the past nations {trap}dismissed the idea that guidance could come through a human like themselves{/trap}. They turned away. And Allah did without them, because {idea}He is free of all need and worthy of all praise{/idea}.
now: The reminder comes from your younger cousin, or a colleague you think is less clever than you. {trap}"Who are you to tell me?"{/trap} {idea}The truth is still the truth, whoever carries it.{/idea}
old: I only take advice from people better than me.
new: Truth from an ordinary person is still truth, and Allah does not need my approval.
try: Think of one piece of good advice you rejected because of who said it. Take it seriously today.

title: Yes, by my Lord, you will be raised.
subtitle: One of three oaths on the resurrection
then: Ibn Kathir notes that this is {idea}the third verse where Allah orders the Prophet ﷺ to swear by his Lord{/idea} that the resurrection is real, along with verses in Yunus and Saba. People will be told of every deed, small or big, and that is easy for Allah.
now: At a funeral, watching the earth go back over the grave, a small voice asks: is that really it? {idea}The answer comes with an oath: yes, by my Lord.{/idea} {reward}The One who made you the first time will do it again.{/reward}
old: Life after death is hard to picture, so maybe it is not real.
new: It is so certain the Prophet ﷺ was told to swear by it, and it is easy for Allah.
try: Next time you pass a graveyard, say a short salam to the people in it and remember you will be raised too.

title: So believe in Allah, His Messenger, and the Light.
subtitle: The Quran is the light to walk by
then: Right after the oath about the resurrection, Allah says: so believe. Ibn Kathir says the Light here is {reward}the Quran{/reward}. {idea}None of your deeds ever escapes His knowledge.{/idea}
now: You walk to the kitchen at night with your phone torch, so you do not trip. {reward}The Quran is that light for the whole road.{/reward} {idea}It does not move your feet for you, but you stop stumbling in the dark.{/idea}
old: The Quran is something I read when I have spare time.
new: The Quran is a light I need to see where I am walking.
try: Before a decision today, open the Quran to any page and read one verse first.

title: The Day of mutual loss and gain.
subtitle: The one day the real winners are known
then: Ibn Kathir says on that Day the first and last generations will stand together in one place. Ibn Abbas said Taghabun is a name for it {reward}because the people of Paradise will have gained over the people of the Fire{/reward}. Muqatil said there is no greater loss and gain than that.
now: Your classmate earns double what you do. Your neighbour seems to win at everything. You feel behind. {idea}The scoreboard you check every day is not the final one.{/idea} {reward}There is a Day when the real gain is shown.{/reward}
old: I am losing because others are getting ahead of me.
new: The real gain and loss are only shown on the Day of Gathering.
try: Today, when you feel behind someone, do one good deed instead of checking their profile.

title: Those who denied His signs: the other side of the Day.
subtitle: The loss that the Day of Taghabun reveals

row.title: in this life
sub: how I meet His signs now

then: This verse completes the picture of the Day of mutual loss and gain. Ibn Kathir pairs it with the verse before: believers enter gardens, while {trap}those who disbelieved and denied Allah's signs{/trap} face the Fire, and {trap}worst indeed is that destination{/trap}.
now: A verse comes up on your feed. A friend shares a reminder. A sunset stops you for a second. {idea}Each one is a sign, and each time you either let it in or wave it away.{/idea} {reward}The Day only shows what you chose here.{/reward}
old: I will deal with the Hereafter when I get there.
new: My place on that Day is shaped by how I treat Allah's signs today.
try: When something reminds you of Allah today, pause for three breaths and let it land.

title: No hardship lands without His permission.
subtitle: And belief guides the heart through it

row.title: it was never going to miss me

then: Ibn Abbas said a believer's heart is guided to certainty: {reward}what reached him would not have missed him, and what missed him would not have reached him{/reward}. Ibn Kathir says Allah compensates the patient with guidance and may replace their loss with the same or better.
now: The phone call from the hospital. The redundancy letter. The miscarriage. {idea}It came by His permission, not by accident.{/idea} {reward}Belief does not make it painless, but He guides the heart that turns to Him.{/reward}
old: Bad things happen randomly and there is no meaning in them.
new: Nothing reaches me without Allah's permission, and He guides the heart that trusts Him.
try: Think of one hard thing you are carrying, and say: inna lillahi wa inna ilayhi raji'un.

title: Obey Allah and the Messenger. His job is to convey.
subtitle: The message, the messenger, and your part
then: Ibn Kathir quotes Az-Zuhri: {idea}from Allah comes the message, on the Messenger is its delivery, and on us is to accept it{/idea}. If people turn away, the Messenger ﷺ has still done his part by conveying it clearly.
now: You have heard the reminders many times, in khutbahs and lectures and from your grandmother. {idea}The message has been delivered.{/idea} {reward}The last step in the chain is yours.{/reward}
old: If I really understood it, I would follow it.
new: The message has reached me clearly. What is left is my response.
try: Pick one thing you already know you should do and have heard many times. Do it once today.

title: No god but Him, so lean on Him.
subtitle: Tawhid ends in trust
then: Ibn Kathir says Allah first states Tawhid, that {idea}He is the One all creation needs and seeks{/idea}, then draws the conclusion: believers should rely on Him. He links it to another verse: there is no god but Him, so take Him as your Trustee.
now: It is 3am and you are running through every way the meeting could go wrong. You have rehearsed it, double-checked it, asked three people. {reward}Now put it down.{/reward} {idea}If there is no god but Him, then He is the One to lean on.{/idea}
old: If I plan enough, I will be safe.
new: I plan, then I lean my full weight on Allah, because there is no one else to lean on.
try: Before your next worry spiral, say hasbunallahu wa ni'mal wakeel once and breathe out.

title: Some of your family can be enemies. Still, forgive.
subtitle: Beware for your faith, then pardon
then: Ibn Abbas said some men in Makkah wanted to migrate, but their families would not let them. When they finally arrived and saw how much others had learned, {trap}they wanted to punish their families{/trap}. This verse came down: {reward}pardon, overlook and forgive{/reward}.
now: Your spouse rolls their eyes when you want to go to the masjid. Your teenager mocks your new habit of praying on time. {idea}Love does not mean following them away from Allah.{/idea} {reward}But it also does not mean holding a grudge.{/reward}
old: If my family held me back from good, they owe me.
new: I guard my faith from my family's pull, and I still forgive them.
try: Think of one family member who made faith harder for you. Forgive them quietly, by name, in a dua.

title: Wealth and children are a test.
subtitle: Even the Prophet ﷺ stopped his sermon for two boys
then: The Prophet ﷺ was giving a sermon when Al-Hasan and Al-Husayn came in, walking and tripping. He came down and picked them up, saying {idea}Allah spoke the truth: your wealth and children are a trial{/idea}. Ibn Kathir says they test who obeys Allah and who does not.
now: Your child wants the new phone everyone has. Your bonus could go to charity or to a bigger car. {idea}The love you feel is real and good.{/idea} {reward}The test is what you do with it.{/reward}
old: My money and my kids are the reward for my hard work.
new: They are gifts and tests, and the greater reward is with Allah.
try: Make a short dua today for your children or your wealth to be a help to you with Allah, not a distraction.

title: Be mindful of Allah as much as you can.
subtitle: Your best effort, not someone else's
then: Ibn Kathir explains "as much as you can" as {reward}what you are able to bear{/reward}, and cites the Prophet ﷺ: when I command you, do as much of it as you can. Giving is {reward}better for yourselves{/reward}, and success belongs to whoever is {trap}saved from their own greed{/trap}.
now: You cannot pray tahajjud every night with a newborn. You cannot give thousands on a student budget. {reward}Allah did not ask for that.{/reward} {idea}He asked for your real best, this week, with what you have.{/idea}
old: If I cannot do it perfectly, there is no point trying.
new: Allah asks for my real best, and greed is what I need saving from.
try: Choose one act you have been avoiding because you cannot do it perfectly, and do a small version today.

title: Lend to Allah, and He multiplies it back.
subtitle: Charity as a loan to the One who never defaults
then: Ibn Kathir says Allah {reward}treats charity as a loan to Himself{/reward}, citing the Qudsi words: who will lend to the One who is neither unjust nor poor? He is Shakur, giving much for little, and Halim, covering and pardoning shortcomings.
now: You hesitate over the donation link. Twenty pounds feels like a lot this month. {reward}It is not gone. It is lent, to the One who pays back more.{/reward} {idea}And He is forbearing with what you could not give.{/idea}
old: Money I give away is money I lose.
new: What I give is a loan to Allah, and He is the best One to owe me.
try: Give one small amount today and say quietly: this is a loan to You, O Allah.

title: Knower of the unseen and the seen.
subtitle: The surah closes on who is watching your effort
then: After asking for taqwa, obedience, charity and a good loan, the surah ends with Allah's names. Ibn Kathir says the meanings were explained before. {idea}He knows the unseen and the seen{/idea}, so no effort or intention is missed.
now: Nobody saw the money you sent, or the patience you showed with your child, or the bad word you held back. {reward}He did.{/reward} {idea}The Mighty, the Wise keeps the record.{/idea}
old: If no one notices my good deeds, they do not really count.
new: Allah sees the unseen and the seen, so nothing I do for Him is wasted.
try: Do one good deed today that only Allah will ever know about.
